subject.size_in_frame: head and hands, face about 0.50 of frame height

second_subject.note: the bitten corner held at the bottom of frame — evidence, not a hero object.

headroom: about 0.16 of frame height, and her hand clapping flat on top of her head fills it inside the shot. The gesture and the frame's ceiling meet.
horizon_eyeline: Low close at 0.18 m, so the lens looks slightly up at her. No architecture in frame. Her eyeline is at 0.44, flicking up and sideways — looking for a change she cannot see.

layers.fg: the cake in her lower hand
layers.mg: her face and the hand clapped on her head
layers.bg: dark hall, one soft amber smear far behind

gaze.note: her eyes go up under her own palm — the sh050 gesture repeated in miniature and at speed. The lead room above her is the answer she is waiting for.

balance: A tight vertical stack — cake at the bottom, face in the middle, hand on top — filling the centre of frame with no space on either side. The frame is as anxious as she is.
leading_lines: Her two forearms come up from the bottom corners and close over her head, making a loop around the whole figure. There is no way out of the shape.
eye_first: The hand slapping onto her head, then her eyes underneath it.
constraint_binding: The bite and the hand happen inside one frame so the anxiety is a single gesture: both hands and her whole head are in shot throughout, no cut and no reframe between the bite and the clap. Two words, fast — the frame is composed tight so the shot can be three seconds and still feel complete.
